page: Amazon Web Services r8g.12xlarge is a memory-optimized server instance powered by the Nitro hypervisor and custom AWS Graviton Neoverse-V2 processors. Utilizing the arm64 architecture, this instance provides 48 dedicated physical cores with a single thread per core, running at a clock speed of 2.8 GHz. The CPU configuration includes 64 KB of L1d cache, 2 MB of L2 cache, and 36 MB of L3 cache. It features 384.0 GB of system memory, yielding a high memory-to-core ratio of 8.0 GB per core. The instance does not include local storage or dedicated GPU hardware, but it provides a baseline network bandwidth of 22 Gbps.

Benchmark data highlights strong memory subsystem performance, with read-only large block memory bandwidth reaching 404.36 GB/sec and write large block bandwidth at 201.11 GB/sec, both placing in the top tier. The passmark memory score and database operations benchmarks also rank in the top tier, with database operations registering 47,285.97. Multi-core CPU performance is strong, as evidenced by a Geekbench multi-core score of 23,531.0 and a stress-ng multi-core score of 81,875.49. However, single-core performance is more moderate, with stress-ng single-core and Geekbench single-core scores falling into the average and strong categories respectively. LLM inference benchmarks show a notable tradeoff: while text generation for medium (7B) and large (70B) models is strong, text generation for smaller models (135M) is relatively weak at 59.89 tokens/sec.

From a cost-efficiency perspective, the r8g.12xlarge delivers high resource density for memory-bound workloads without the overhead of hyperthreading, as each of the 48 vCPUs maps to a dedicated physical core. The lack of bundled local storage means storage-heavy workloads must rely on network-attached options, which may impact overall I/O latency. Given its top-tier memory bandwidth and database operation benchmarks, this instance is highly suited for memory-intensive databases, in-memory caching systems like Redis, large-scale data compilation, and static web serving.
